messages:
cheng: FYI I'm opening a TF module change for the gpupool to support a spot/reserved conditional and a provider alias cleanup.
Sasha: 👍 what's the var name change? last time we had trouble with consumers using the old name.
cheng: renaming `instance_tier` -> `instance_class` (more generic). will add a compatibility shim for one release.
paul: please add a clear deprecation message in the README and emit a plan-time warning in the CI job.
maria: also need to confirm KMS alias handling — cross-account aliasing was causing plan diffs for us last month.
cheng: yes. new module will accept `kms_alias_id` OR `kms_alias_name` and only build the ARN if alias_name is set. snippet:
```hcl
variable "kms_alias_name" { type = string; default = "" }
locals { kms_alias_arn = length(var.kms_alias_name) > 0 ? "arn:aws:kms:${var.region}:${var.account_id}:alias/${var.kms_alias_name}" : var.kms_alias_id }
```
Sasha: That logic should avoid terraform thinking the alias changed when provider alias or account is different. good call.
alex: small ops question — will provider aliases (for shared infra account) be required now? we've seen drift when people forget to set `provider = aws.shared` in their env.
cheng: plan is to keep provider alias optional. if users don't set it, module uses the default provider. if they set `use_shared_provider = true` it will require `providers = { aws = aws.shared }` in the root module. docs will include example.
paul: can we add an automated linter in the gitops pipeline that rejects module usage without the `use_shared_provider` flag when `account_id` != root account? to prevent silent drift.
maria: +1. also we should add a pre-merge TF plan reviewer job to annotate diffs that touch KMS/iam/gpupool resources.
gitops-bot: PR #789: terraform plan completed with 3 changes. See artifacts link: https://ci.internal/reports/789/plan
cheng: plan shows provider alias import is a noop but kms alias will be created in 1 env — that's expected for staging run.
Sasha: rollout strategy? We Should canary the module bump across a few small clusters first (non-prod), then prod gpufleet.
paul: propose: (1) merge with shim, (2) run for 48h in staging, (3) promote to preprod for 24h, (4) schedule prod window and have rollback tfstate snapshot.
alex: ops runbook: if nodes fail to join after apply, revert module to previous tag and run `terraform apply -target=module.gpupool` then escalate.
maria: also add a sentinel check in the CI that queries cluster health post-apply: `kubectl get nodes` + check for Failed statuses.
cheng: I've pushed branch `gpupool/instance-class-kms-shim` and created PR with checklist. tagging @Sasha @paul for approvals.
Sasha: reviewing now.
deploy-bot: canary deploy pipeline triggered for pr-789 to cluster: staging-gpufleet-02
paul: note on cost — spot conditional will reduce cost ~30% for batch workloads. add a note in the PR about cost impact and a metric to watch (GPU-hours and preempt rate).
cheng: added COST.md in module with estimated delta and a recommended fallback to reserved if preempt rate > 20%.
Sasha: lgtm with one comment about variable naming. after that I'll approve and we can start the staged rollout.
cheng: thanks — will address and re-run plan. will post status updates in this thread.
